blocking.title: The workerTransport prescriptions are still parsed away — round-1 blocking finding 1 closed for the process block, left open verbatim for the transport block
blocking.detail: WorkerTransportWire reads exactly one field: kind. verifyOsPeer, runBoundToken and hostLoopbackAllowed are deserialized into nothing, reach no decision, and produce no refusal. resolve_controls touches the transport only to test kind against CLOSED_TRANSPORT_KINDS. Both fields are SILENTLY IGNORED — not enforced, not refused, not documented as moot. Nothing generates, injects or verifies any run-bound token, and no peer credential is read. Either the socketpair is argued in code and manifest to subsume both fields, or a profile prescribing them on a mechanism that implements neither must be refused.

blocking.title: effectiveProfileDigest is an unconditional echo of the requested digest, so the attestation asserts as effective five profile blocks this stage does not implement
blocking.detail: run.rs passes resolved.digest() as BOTH requested and effective, and resolve_profile has already proven declared == requested: the two fields are the same string on every run that signs — structurally, not situationally. attestation.rs's own doc claims the opposite. The document bound as effective still contains filesystem, workerTransport, providerGateway, privilegedToolBroker and operationalLogs, none of which any code path applies. Removing filesystem_confinement from effectiveControls was right, but the same claim still stands in the field that binds the whole document.

blocking.title: maxDurationSeconds is still not a bound, and the process-group reap is host-conditional and untested
blocking.detail: (a) sender.write_all(payload) runs BEFORE the duration clock starts and no write timeout is set — a worker that never reads stdin blocks the harness indefinitely. (b) child.wait() after the loop is unbounded, and the EOF and read-error paths reach it without reaping. (c) reap hardcodes /bin/kill with no existence check while every other tool goes through tool_path; when it is absent the code falls through to the direct-child kill round 1 rejected, with no refusal and an identical attestation. (d) No test exercises the fix: the only duration test uses an unprivileged plan, so kills_process_group() is false and it tests the pre-fix path; the e2e runs /bin/cat. No test spawns a grandchild under setsid and asserts it dies.

major.title: sandboxEngineManifest is still caller-asserted and never verified; a third hand-maintained copy of the same fact was added
major.detail: SandboxEngineWire reads required_capabilities and nothing else: the pinned manifest id, digest, mediaType and denyOnMissing are deserialized away. run_confined_attested copies the caller's ArtifactRef verbatim into the signature with no comparison against the profile's pin and no read of the on-disk manifest. Three facts are now duplicated by hand with no gate (manifest sha256, profile pin, test constant), plus ENGINE_CAPABILITIES vs the manifest's capabilities array. All four are consistent today; nothing asserts any of them.

major.title: The attestation binds capability labels, never the mechanism that produced them
major.detail: effectiveControls is computed from HostFacts before the wrapper chain is planned, so it describes what the host was judged capable of, not what the argv applied. Nothing binds setsid/prlimit/setpriv, their paths, flags, target uid/gid or nproc value. Two hosts applying materially different confinement emit byte-identical attestations. The predicates also do not name their own mechanisms: resource_limits is gated on setpriv_present though prlimit applies it.

major.title: The dedicated identity's GID is fabricated
major.detail: The e2e probes id -u and returns (uid, uid) — it never queries id -g. useradd --system allocates UID and GID from independent counters; --regid=<uid> then places the worker in whatever unrelated group holds that GID. The harness accepts any caller-supplied non-zero pair and never verifies the ids exist, that the gid is the uid's primary group, or that they are not shared.

major.title: The public API exports a fully unconfined spawn path, and the tests institutionalize it
major.detail: plan_wrapper_chain returns Ok with an EMPTY prefix when every prescription field is false/zero; spawn_confined then execs directly. lib.rs exports the constructors, so a consumer composes an unconfined run in four lines with no attestation and no refusal. The invariant lives entirely in the external JSON schema; the Rust types encode none of it.

major.title: A control firing is reported as a worker fault, and the matrix has no code for the duration bound
major.detail: exit_ok folds timed_out into failure and run.rs turns it into RunError::WorkerFault, whose doc says a worker fault is a worker that failed inside honoured controls. A timeout is the opposite. The 13-code matrix has no duration-bound member, so the most attestation-worthy outcome — the confinement killed the worker — produces no signed evidence at all.

minor.title: The guard's hardening was applied to one of its two checkers
minor.detail: FORBIDDEN_SOURCE_PATTERNS is consumed only by forbiddenEverywhere. forbiddenOutsideHost still tests plain source.includes over std::process, std::fs, std::os::unix::net, std::thread, std::time, so `use std::{fs, process};` in a pure module passes.

minor.title: The filesystem prescription is largely parsed away and never checked against the run's workspace
minor.detail: workspaceRoot, canonicalizePaths, resolveSymlinks, symlinkPolicy and copyIgnoredFiles are dropped; run_confined_attested never compares the caller's workspace against the profile's declared workspaceRoot. The three parsed lists feed evaluate_path_access, which no run path calls.

minor.title: maxProcesses = 0 silently disables the process ceiling
minor.detail: The prlimit wrapper is gated on max_processes > 0; zero — the strictest reading — is implemented as no bound at all, with no refusal.

minor.title: Host-fact probing is inconsistent with the crate's own tool-resolution discipline
minor.detail: gather_host_facts hardcodes /usr/bin/id and reap hardcodes /bin/kill, while tool_path probes /usr/bin then /bin for the other three. Both should go through tool_path, and kill should become a HostFact.

minor.title: The mechanically-enforced boundary is narrower than lib.rs claims
minor.detail: The guard globs crates/agent-harness/src/**/*.rs only; tests/ is unscanned. Legitimate, but the claim should be scoped to src/.

nonBlocking.title: The recomputed fixture digests are correct
nonBlocking.detail: JCS(local-process minus profileDigest) = de9b3af5…, equal to the declared value; raw sha256 of the engine manifest = db11edba…, equal to the profile pin and the test constant; the manifest's 4 capabilities equal ENGINE_CAPABILITIES and the profile's 3 required are a subset. Only the pin and the capability equality are ungated.

nonBlocking.title: Round-1 minor items other than the guard are genuinely closed
nonBlocking.detail: chrono is gone from the crate and from the allowlist, now an upper bound rather than a requiredlist; the e2e derives the platform from cfg!(target_arch); CI's identity creation is idempotent and the privileged step builds unprivileged then runs only the prebuilt binary under sudo with no preserved PATH.

nonBlocking.title: RLIMIT_NPROC is a per-UID ceiling, not a per-run one
nonBlocking.detail: prlimit --nproc bounds processes owned by the real UID system-wide, and the dedicated identity is caller-nominated and reusable: concurrent runs share one ceiling. Second-order, setpriv's setuid can fail with EAGAIN once that uid holds the ceiling — fail-closed, but an availability coupling between unrelated runs.

nonBlocking.title: The environment-clearing test can pass for the wrong reason
nonBlocking.detail: The test runs /bin/sh -c env under env_clear and asserts the absence of PATH= and HOME=. Common shells synthesize a default PATH, so on some hosts this asserts shell behaviour. Assert emptiness instead.

nonBlocking.title: The closed dependency allowlist forces process spawning for facts the OS could answer
nonBlocking.detail: With no libc the harness execs /usr/bin/id for its own euid and /bin/kill to signal a group. A defensible sovereignty trade, but it converts two syscalls into two external-binary dependencies, each a fail-open or fail-closed hinge. Worth an explicit architecture note.

nonBlocking.title: Worktree unmodified
nonBlocking.detail: git status --porcelain returned empty at the start and end of the pass; no cargo or bun was run.

residualRisks: The locked schema is not vendored in this worktree, so every const-true argument in comments and commit messages is unverifiable in a static pass.

The whole confinement rests on util-linux flag semantics this pass could not execute: whether the installed setpriv honours --ambient-caps/--bounding-set, whether --reuid sets the saved uid, whether setsid forks in the runner's process-group state. The argv shape and ordering are correct, but no test observes the resulting process's credentials or capability sets after exec.

No evidence exists that a confined run ever survived a real bound: the e2e worker is /bin/cat, which exits before any control fires. The first-confined-execution claim rests on an attestation whose effectiveControls the harness computed from its own host facts, not on any observation of the confined process.

The bootstrap identity persists on the runner across jobs and is shared by every run on that machine; combined with the per-UID RLIMIT_NPROC and the fabricated GID, one run's behaviour can affect another's.
Refusals and bound-firings produce no signed artifact, so the evidentiary chain covers only successful runs.
